        (f.fiberToSpecResidueField t).appTop := Scheme.Hom.appLE_eq_app _

      (Scheme.ΓSpecIso ((Spec R).residueField t)).hom_inv_id
    simp only [CommRingCat.hom_comp, RingHom.comp_apply, CommRingCat.hom_id,
      RingHom.id_apply] at h₁

theorem fiberRank_gammaTop_eq_fiberH0_of_isFinite_schematicSupport
    {R : CommRingCat.{u}} {X : Scheme.{u}} (f : X ⟶ Spec R)
    (F : X.Modules) [F.IsQuasicoherent]
    (hfin : IsFinite (schematicSupportι F ≫ f)) (t : PrimeSpectrum R) :
    Module.finrank t.asIdeal.ResidueField
        (t.asIdeal.Fiber
          Γ((pushforward f).obj F, (⊤ : (Spec R).Opens))) =
      f.fiberH0 F t :=
  fiberRank_gammaTop_eq_fiberH0_of_iso f F t
    (pullbackPushforwardIso_of_isFinite_schematicSupport
      (IsPullback.of_hasPullback f
        ((Spec R).fromSpecResidueField (t : Spec R))) F hfin)

end Modules

namespace DivFamily

/-- On an affine test base, a finite-flat divisor pushforward is locally free
of the divisor's fibre degree.  The proof supplies finite presentation and
projectivity from the existing pushforward producers; the rank is computed by
the finite-support base-change bridge above, not assumed separately. -/
theorem pushforward_isLocallyFreeOfRank
    {R : CommRingCat.{u}} {S X : Scheme.{u}} {π : X ⟶ S}
    [IsProper π] (f : Spec R ⟶ S) [IsNoetherianRing R]
    (x : DivFamily π (Over.mk f))
    [LocallyQuasiFinite
      (Modules.schematicSupportι x.F ≫ pullback.snd π f)]
    {d : ℕ} (hx : x.HasFiberDeg d) :
    SheafOfModules.IsLocallyFreeOfRank
      ((Modules.pushforward (pullback.snd π f)).obj x.F) d := by
  let q := pullback.snd π f
  let M := (Modules.pushforward q).obj x.F
  haveI : M.IsFinitePresentation := x.isFinitePresentation_pushforward
  haveI : M.IsQuasicoherent := inferInstance
  have hfin : Module.Finite R Γ(M, (⊤ : (Spec R).Opens)) :=
    Modules.module_finite_sections_of_isFinitePresentation M
      ⟨⊤, isAffineOpen_top (Spec R)⟩
  have hflat : Module.Flat R Γ(M, (⊤ : (Spec R).Opens)) :=
    Modules.flat_sections_of_coherentSheafFlat_id
      x.coherentSheafFlat_id_pushforward (isAffineOpen_top (Spec R))
  letI : Module.Finite R Γ(M, (⊤ : (Spec R).Opens)) := hfin
  letI : Module.Flat R Γ(M, (⊤ : (Spec R).Opens)) := hflat
  letI : Module.FinitePresentation R Γ(M, (⊤ : (Spec R).Opens)) :=
    Module.finitePresentation_of_finite R _
  letI : Module.Projective R Γ(M, (⊤ : (Spec R).Opens)) :=
    Module.Flat.projective_of_finitePresentation
  apply Modules.isLocallyFreeOfRank_of_finite_projective_sections M hfin inferInstance
  intro t
  change Module.rankAtStalk Γ(M, (⊤ : (Spec R).Opens)) t = d
  rw [Module.rankAtStalk_eq]
  haveI : IsProper (Modules.schematicSupportι x.F ≫ q) := x.properSupport
  have hsupport : IsFinite (Modules.schematicSupportι x.F ≫ q) :=
    IsFinite.of_isProper_of_locallyQuasiFinite _
  exact (Modules.fiberRank_gammaTop_eq_fiberH0_of_isFinite_schematicSupport
    q x.F hsupport t).trans (hx t)

end DivFamily

end Scheme

    (sq : IsPullback g' f' f g) (F : X.Modules) [F.IsQuasicoherent]
    (hfin : IsFinite (schematicSupportι F ≫ f)) :
    (pullback g).obj ((pushforward f).obj F) ≅

    inferInstanceAs (IsAffineHom F.annihilator.subschemeι)
  haveI : IsFinite (i ≫ f) := hfin
  haveI : IsAffineHom (i ≫ f) := inferInstance

    13	/-!
    14	# The divisor-to-Grassmannian comparison
    15	
    16	This file begins campaign milestone D2': a divisor family is twisted by a fixed
    17	module on the curve, and the pullback--pushforward base-change map followed by
    18	the divisor quotient gives the canonical evaluation morphism used by the
    19	Grassmannian construction.
    20	
    21	The definitions in the first section are unconditional.  In particular,
    22	`DivFamily.grassmannianEval` exists before the Riemann--Roch argument proves it
    23	epimorphic.  Keeping the map separate from its eventual `Epi` proof prevents
    24	uniform generation from becoming an assumption in the definition of the
    25	comparison.
    26	
    27	The second section records two affine algebra bridges used to turn finite flat
    28	pushforwards into the rank-indexed local-freeness predicate expected by
    29	`Scheme.LocallyFreeQuotient`.  They do not introduce a representability gate:
    30	their inputs are ordinary finite-presentation, finiteness, and projectivity
    31	properties with producers elsewhere in the Picard development.
    32	-/

    35	
    36	universe u

    48	private lemma map_tensorHom_comp2 {C D : Type*} [Category C] [MonoidalCategory C]
    49	    [Category D] (F : C ⥤ D) {a₀ a₁ a₂ b₀ b₁ b₂ : C}
    50	    (a : a₀ ⟶ a₁) (b : a₁ ⟶ a₂) (d : b₀ ⟶ b₁) (e : b₁ ⟶ b₂) :
    51	    F.map (MonoidalCategory.tensorHom a d) ≫ F.map (MonoidalCategory.tensorHom b e) =
    52	      F.map (MonoidalCategory.tensorHom (a ≫ b) (d ≫ e)) := by
    53	  rw [← F.map_comp, MonoidalCategory.tensorHom_comp_tensorHom]

    55	/-- The twist of the divisor structure sheaf by a module on the original
    56	family.  For the D2' embedding, `L` is the chosen sufficiently positive
    57	projective twist. -/
    58	noncomputable def twist (L : X.Modules) (x : DivFamily π T) :
    59	    (pullback π T.hom).Modules :=
    60	  Modules.tensorObj ((Modules.pullback (pullback.fst π T.hom)).obj L) x.F
    61	
    62	/-- Tensor the divisor quotient `O -> O_D` with the pulled-back twist. -/
    63	noncomputable def twistQuotientMap (L : X.Modules) (x : DivFamily π T) :
    64	    (Modules.pullback (pullback.fst π T.hom)).obj L ⟶ x.twist L :=
    65	  (Modules.tensorObj_right_unitor _).inv ≫
    66	    Modules.tensorObj_functoriality (𝟙 _)
    67	      ((Modules.pullbackUnitIso (pullback.fst π T.hom)).inv ≫ x.q)
    68	
    69	/-- Equivalent divisor families have isomorphic twists, compatibly with the
    70	twisted quotient maps.  This is the representative-level descent input for
    71	the D2' Grassmannian comparison. -/
    72	lemma twistQuotientMap_rel (L : X.Modules) {x y : DivFamily π T} (h : x.Rel y) :
    73	    ∃ f : x.twist L ≅ y.twist L,
    74	      x.twistQuotientMap L ≫ f.hom = y.twistQuotientMap L := by
    75	  obtain ⟨f, hf⟩ := h
    76	  refine ⟨Modules.tensorObjIsoOfIso (Iso.refl _) f, ?_⟩
    77	  change ((Modules.tensorObj_right_unitor _).inv ≫
    78	      Modules.tensorObj_functoriality (𝟙 _)
    79	        ((Modules.pullbackUnitIso (pullback.fst π T.hom)).inv ≫ x.q)) ≫
    80	      Modules.tensorObj_functoriality (𝟙 _) f.hom =
    81	    (Modules.tensorObj_right_unitor _).inv ≫
    82	      Modules.tensorObj_functoriality (𝟙 _)
    83	        ((Modules.pullbackUnitIso (pullback.fst π T.hom)).inv ≫ y.q)
    84	  rw [Category.assoc]
    85	  rw [show Modules.tensorObj_functoriality (𝟙 _) _ ≫
    86	        Modules.tensorObj_functoriality (𝟙 _) f.hom =
    87	      Modules.tensorObj_functoriality ((𝟙 _) ≫ (𝟙 _))
    88	        (((Modules.pullbackUnitIso (pullback.fst π T.hom)).inv ≫ x.q) ≫ f.hom) by
    89	    simp only [Modules.tensorObj_functoriality]
    90	    exact map_tensorHom_comp2
    91	      (C := _root_.PresheafOfModules
    92	        ((pullback π T.hom).presheaf ⋙ forget₂ CommRingCat RingCat))
    93	      _ _ _ _ _]
    94	  simp only [Category.id_comp]
    95	  rw [Category.assoc, hf]

    97	/-- The canonical D2' evaluation morphism.
    98	
    99	It first base-changes `π_* L` from `S` to `T`, then pushes forward the twisted
   100	divisor quotient along `X_T -> T`.  Uniform Riemann--Roch will prove that this
   101	map is an epimorphism for a sufficiently positive `L`; no such conclusion is
   102	built into the definition. -/
   103	noncomputable def grassmannianEval (L : X.Modules) (x : DivFamily π T) :
   104	    (Modules.pullback T.hom).obj ((Modules.pushforward π).obj L) ⟶
   105	      (Modules.pushforward (pullback.snd π T.hom)).obj (x.twist L) :=
   106	  pushforwardBaseChangeMap π T.hom (pullback.snd π T.hom)
   107	      (pullback.fst π T.hom) pullback.condition L ≫
   108	    (Modules.pushforward (pullback.snd π T.hom)).map (x.twistQuotientMap L)
   109	
   110	/-- Equivalent divisor families have isomorphic evaluation targets, and the
   111	isomorphism commutes with the D2' evaluation maps. -/
   112	lemma grassmannianEval_rel (L : X.Modules) {x y : DivFamily π T} (h : x.Rel y) :
   113	    ∃ f : (Modules.pushforward (pullback.snd π T.hom)).obj (x.twist L) ≅
   114	        (Modules.pushforward (pullback.snd π T.hom)).obj (y.twist L),
   115	      x.grassmannianEval L ≫ f.hom = y.grassmannianEval L := by
   116	  obtain ⟨f, hf⟩ := twistQuotientMap_rel L h
   117	  refine ⟨(Modules.pushforward (pullback.snd π T.hom)).mapIso f, ?_⟩
   118	  change (pushforwardBaseChangeMap π T.hom (pullback.snd π T.hom)
   119	      (pullback.fst π T.hom) pullback.condition L ≫
   120	        (Modules.pushforward (pullback.snd π T.hom)).map (x.twistQuotientMap L)) ≫
   121	      (Modules.pushforward (pullback.snd π T.hom)).map f.hom =
   122	    pushforwardBaseChangeMap π T.hom (pullback.snd π T.hom)
   123	      (pullback.fst π T.hom) pullback.condition L ≫
   124	        (Modules.pushforward (pullback.snd π T.hom)).map (y.twistQuotientMap L)
   125	  rw [Category.assoc, ← Functor.map_comp, hf]

   127	/-- Epimorphy of the D2' evaluation map is invariant under
   128	`DivFamily.Rel`. -/
   129	lemma grassmannianEval_epi_of_rel (L : X.Modules) {x y : DivFamily π T}
   130	    (h : x.Rel y) (hx : Epi (x.grassmannianEval L)) :
   131	    Epi (y.grassmannianEval L) := by
   132	  obtain ⟨f, hf⟩ := grassmannianEval_rel L h
   133	  letI := hx
   134	  rw [← hf]
   135	  infer_instance

   138	invariant under `DivFamily.Rel`. -/
   139	lemma grassmannianTarget_isLocallyFreeOfRank_of_rel
   140	    (L : X.Modules) {x y : DivFamily π T} (hxy : x.Rel y) {d : ℕ}
   141	    (hx : SheafOfModules.IsLocallyFreeOfRank
   142	      ((Modules.pushforward (pullback.snd π T.hom)).obj (x.twist L)) d) :
   143	    SheafOfModules.IsLocallyFreeOfRank
   144	      ((Modules.pushforward (pullback.snd π T.hom)).obj (y.twist L)) d := by
   145	  obtain ⟨f, _⟩ := grassmannianEval_rel L hxy
   146	  obtain ⟨ι, U, hU, hloc⟩ := hx
   147	  exact ⟨ι, U, hU, fun i =>
   148	    ⟨(Modules.pullback (U i).ι).mapIso f.symm ≪≫ (hloc i).some⟩⟩
   149

   151	This keeps the base-change and divisor-quotient obligations separate, so a
   152	later uniform-generation proof can discharge only the factor it actually
   153	proves. -/
   154	theorem grassmannianEval_epi (L : X.Modules) (x : DivFamily π T)
   155	    (hbase : Epi (pushforwardBaseChangeMap π T.hom
   156	      (pullback.snd π T.hom) (pullback.fst π T.hom) pullback.condition L))
   157	    (hquot : Epi ((Modules.pushforward (pullback.snd π T.hom)).map
   158	      (x.twistQuotientMap L))) :
   159	    Epi (x.grassmannianEval L) := by
   160	  letI := hbase

   162	  dsimp [grassmannianEval]

   165	/-- **The conditional D2' quotient datum.**  Once the evaluation map is an
   166	epimorphism and its target has constant locally-free rank `d`, it is exactly a
   167	rank-`d` locally free quotient of the pulled-back pushforward of `L`.
   168	
   169	The two arguments are deliberately explicit: the evaluation map is the
   170	uniform-generation obligation, while the locally-free target is the
   171	finite/projective/rank obligation.  This constructor packages those genuine
   172	outputs without introducing a class or an instance that could hide either one.
   173	-/
   174	noncomputable def grassmannianQuotient (L : X.Modules) (x : DivFamily π T)
   175	    [IsLocallyNoetherian S] {d : ℕ} (hEpi : Epi (x.grassmannianEval L))
   176	    (hLocFree : SheafOfModules.IsLocallyFreeOfRank
   177	      ((Modules.pushforward (pullback.snd π T.hom)).obj (x.twist L)) d) :
   178	    LocallyFreeQuotient ((Modules.pushforward π).obj L) d T := by
   179	  letI := hEpi
   180	  exact {
   181	    F := (Modules.pushforward (pullback.snd π T.hom)).obj (x.twist L)
   182	    q := x.grassmannianEval L
   183	    epi := inferInstance
   184	    locFree := hLocFree }

    10	/-!
    11	# Pushing a divisor family down to the base, flatly
    12	
    13	Campaign milestone **D3'** (`informal/pic-representability-campaign.md:305`) asks
    14	for the locus over which a Grassmannian `T`-point arises from a degree-`d`
    15	`DivFamily` to be locally closed *universally*, by extending
    16	`AlgebraicGeometry.flatLocusStratification_universal`
    17	(`Picard/FlatteningStratificationUniversal.lean`) "to the family `C × G → G`".
    18	
    19	This file supplies the object that extension has to be about, and records why the
    20	extension has to be phrased this way rather than by relativising the machine.
    21	
    22	## The shape of the reduction, and why it is forced
    23	
    24	`flatLocusStratification_universal` is stated for a module **on the base**,
    25	`F : S.Modules`, with `π = 𝟙 S`. That is not an accident of its proof that a
    26	later session can relax: the whole stratification machine is built on
    27	`Scheme.Modules.pointRank : (X : Scheme) → X.Modules → ↥X → ℕ`, which takes a
    28	module on *one* scheme and a point of *that* scheme. There is no relative
    29	`pointRank` over a morphism, and `chartLocus`, `rankStratum`,
    30	`isOpen_pointRank_pullback_eq` and `existsUnique_factor_rankStratum` all inherit
    31	that shape. So a general-`π` universal property cannot be obtained by adding a
    32	`π` to those statements; the family has to be *moved to the base* first.
    33	
    34	For a divisor family that move is available, and cheaply, because a relative
    35	effective divisor is finite over the base — where a general proper family is not.
    36	Concretely: `Scheme.Modules.HasProperSupport` is by definition
    37	`IsProper (schematicSupportι F ≫ f)` (`Picard/QuotScheme.lean`), and
    38	`DivFamily.properSupport` is exactly that datum for `f = pullback.snd π T.hom`.
    39	A proper *quasi-finite* morphism is finite (`IsFinite.of_isProper_of_locallyQuasiFinite`),
    40	hence affine, and `Scheme.CoherentSheafFlat` transfers along an affine
    41	pushforward. Since `O_D` is the pushforward of its own restriction to the support
    42	(`schematicSupportDescentIso`), the family's flatness over `T` becomes flatness of
    43	`q_* O_D` over `T` *itself* — the `n = 0` shape the universal property consumes.
    44	
    45	## What is proved here, and what is assumed
    46	
    47	* `Scheme.CoherentSheafFlat.of_pushforward_of_isAffineHom` — the **converse** of
    48	  `Scheme.CoherentSheafFlat.pushforward_of_isAffineHom`
    49	  (`Picard/RigidPushforwardTransfer.lean`), which did not exist. Both directions
    50	  are the same chart computation read in opposite directions; the content is that
    51	  the two `Γ(T, U)`-module structures on `Γ(F, π ⁻¹ᵁ V)` agree, which is
    52	  `Scheme.Hom.appLE_comp_appLE`.
    53	
    54	* `Scheme.DivFamily.coherentSheafFlat_id_pushforward` — for a divisor family whose
    55	  divisor is quasi-finite over the base, `q_* O_D` is flat over `T` in the
    56	  `CoherentSheafFlat (𝟙 T.left)` sense.
    57	
    58	**The quasi-finiteness is a hypothesis, not a theorem, and this file does not
    59	pretend otherwise.** `LocallyQuasiFinite (schematicSupportι x.F ≫ pullback.snd π T.hom)`
    60	says the divisor `D ⊆ X_T` has finite fibres over `T`. Mathematically it is
    61	relative-dimension-1 content: on the curve fibre `C_t`, `D_t` is the zero scheme
    62	of a regular section of an invertible ideal, hence `0`-dimensional. It has no
    63	producer in this project, and `LocallyQuasiFinite` occurs nowhere else in
    64	`Picard/`. It is stated as an instance binder so that a later producer discharges
    65	every consumer at once.
    66	
    67	Worth recording for whoever prices the next step: this hypothesis is *cleaner*
    68	than the one it replaces. `Picard/DivDegree.lean` gates its clopen degree
    69	decomposition on `HasLocallyConstantDivDeg`, a `Prop`-class carrying local
    70	constancy of `fiberDeg` as an assumption and also without a producer. With
    71	quasi-finiteness instead, local constancy is downstream of a stratification
    72	theorem rather than assumed beside it — the same missing geometry, but bought
    73	once and in a form the machine can use.
    74	
    75	## What remains for D3'
    76	
    77	`flatLocusStratification_universal` has exactly **two** binders:
    78	`[IsNoetherian S]` and `[F.IsFinitePresentation]`. `IsQuasicoherent` is a mathlib
    79	instance *from* finite presentation, so it is not a separate requirement;
    80	`DivFamily.isQuasicoherent_pushforward` below is kept because it is the cheap half
    81	and is wanted in its own right, not because `:876` asks for it.
    82	
    83	Finite presentation of `q_* O_D` is `DivFamily.isFinitePresentation_pushforward`,
    84	proved here. `isFinitePresentation_of_finite_sections`
    85	(`Picard/RigidPushforwardTransfer.lean`) reduces it to `Module.Finite Γ(T,V)
    86	Γ(q_* O_D, V)` on affine `V`, and that tower is:
    87	
    88	* `Module.Finite Γ(T,V) Γ(D,W)` for `W := (i ≫ q) ⁻¹ᵁ V`, from
    89	  `IsFinite.finite_app` — this is where the finiteness of the support map is spent,
    90	  and it is exactly what quasi-finiteness bought;
    91	* `Module.Finite Γ(D,W) Γ(N,W)` from `finite_sections_preimage_of_isAffineHom`
    92	  together with `isFinitePresentation_pullback_schematicSupportι`;
    93	* the two compose by `Module.Finite.trans`, and the result transports back across
    94	  `schematicSupportDescentIso` because `Γ(q_* F, V) = Γ(F, q ⁻¹ᵁ V)` and
    95	  `Γ(i_* N, q ⁻¹ᵁ V) = Γ(N, (i ≫ q) ⁻¹ᵁ V)` are both `rfl`, and the native
    96	  `Γ(T,V)`-action on `Γ(q_* F, V)` *is* `compHom` along `q.app V`, also `rfl`. The
    97	  semilinearity is `Scheme.Modules.Hom.app_smul`.
    98	
    99	## What remains for D3'
   100	
   101	Two things, and neither is supplied here.
   102	
   103	**A stated bridge, not a free fit.** `:876` stratifies a module on the base and
   104	quantifies its universal property over test morphisms `φ : T' ⟶ S`; its antecedent
   105	asks for `CoherentSheafFlat (𝟙 T') ((Modules.pullback φ).obj F)`. What
   106	`coherentSheafFlat_id_pushforward` gives is the `φ = 𝟙` case *before* the identity
   107	pullback is reduced, so feeding it needs
   108	`(Scheme.Modules.pullbackId T.left).app _` through `coherentSheafFlat_of_iso` —
   109	one line, but a line, and it discharges the `φ = 𝟙` **instance** rather than the
   110	antecedent as a family. Whether that instance is what D3' needs is not settled in
   111	this file and should be settled before D3' is priced as "inputs done".
   112	
   113	**The `∃!` statement about the Grassmannian locus itself**, which is D3' proper.
   114	
   115	Nothing in this file closes D3'.
   116	
   117	## Honest status of every antecedent
   118	
   119	`Scheme.DivFamily` itself has **no producer anywhere in this project** — 135
   120	mention sites, all consumers (measured 2026-07-29, inbox `I-0957`). So the
   121	theorems here, like the rest of Cluster D', are true statements about a carrier
   122	nobody has yet inhabited; that is a property of the cluster, not of this file, and
   123	it is recorded rather than hidden. The `LocallyQuasiFinite` binder has no producer
   124	either, and is *not* derivable from `DivFamily`'s other fields (kernel-checked),
   125	so it is genuine content and not a restatement of `properSupport`.
   126	-/

   188	/-- **The pushforward of `O_D` is flat over the base itself.**
   189	
   190	For a divisor family `x` whose divisor is quasi-finite over `T`, the pushforward

   192	`CoherentSheafFlat (𝟙 T.left)` sense.

   194	This is the `n = 0` shape, but **not literally what
   195	`AlgebraicGeometry.flatLocusStratification_universal` asks for**: its antecedent

   199	Route: `x.properSupport` is `IsProper (i ≫ q)` by definition, so with

   205	theorem Scheme.DivFamily.coherentSheafFlat_id_pushforward
   206	    {S X : Scheme.{u}} {π : X ⟶ S} {T : Over S} (x : Scheme.DivFamily π T)
   207	    [LocallyQuasiFinite
   208	      (Scheme.Modules.schematicSupportι x.F ≫ pullback.snd π T.hom)] :
   209	    Scheme.CoherentSheafFlat (𝟙 (T.left : Scheme.{u}))
   210	      ((Scheme.Modules.pushforward (pullback.snd π T.hom)).obj x.F) := by
   211	  letI := x.isFinitePresentation
   212	  haveI : x.F.IsQuasicoherent := inferInstance
   213	  set q := pullback.snd π T.hom with hq
   214	  set i := Scheme.Modules.schematicSupportι x.F with hi
   215	  -- `i ≫ q` is proper by the divisor family's own support datum, hence finite,
   216	  -- hence affine.
   217	  haveI : IsProper (i ≫ q) := x.properSupport
   218	  haveI : IsFinite (i ≫ q) := IsFinite.of_isProper_of_locallyQuasiFinite _
   219	  haveI : IsAffineHom (i ≫ q) := inferInstance
   220	  haveI : IsAffineHom i :=
   221	    inferInstanceAs (IsAffineHom (Scheme.Modules.annihilator x.F).subschemeι)
   222	  -- present `O_D` as `i_*` of its restriction to the support
   223	  set N := (Scheme.Modules.pullback i).obj x.F with hN
   224	  have hdesc : x.F ≅ (Scheme.Modules.pushforward i).obj N :=
   225	    Scheme.Modules.schematicSupportDescentIso x.F
   226	  haveI : N.IsQuasicoherent := pullback_isQuasicoherent_hom i x.F inferInstance
   227	  -- flatness of `i_* N` over `T`, transported from the family's flatness
   228	  have h1 : Scheme.CoherentSheafFlat q ((Scheme.Modules.pushforward i).obj N) :=
   229	    coherentSheafFlat_of_iso q hdesc x.flat
   230	  -- descend it to `N` along the affine `i`
   231	  have h2 : Scheme.CoherentSheafFlat (i ≫ q) N :=
   232	    Scheme.CoherentSheafFlat.of_pushforward_of_isAffineHom i q N h1
   233	  -- push forward along the affine `i ≫ q`, over the identity of the base
   234	  have h3 : Scheme.CoherentSheafFlat (𝟙 (T.left : Scheme.{u}))
   235	      ((Scheme.Modules.pushforward (i ≫ q)).obj N) :=
   236	    Scheme.CoherentSheafFlat.pushforward_of_isAffineHom (i ≫ q)
   237	      (𝟙 (T.left : Scheme.{u})) N (by rwa [Category.comp_id])
   238	  -- and identify `(i ≫ q)_* N ≅ q_* (i_* N) ≅ q_* O_D`

   240	  exact coherentSheafFlat_of_iso (𝟙 (T.left : Scheme.{u}))
   241	    ((Scheme.Modules.pushforwardComp i q).app N ≪≫
   242	      (Scheme.Modules.pushforward q).mapIso hdesc.symm) h3 hU hV eV

   254	theorem Scheme.DivFamily.isQuasicoherent_pushforward
   255	    {S X : Scheme.{u}} {π : X ⟶ S} [IsProper π] {T : Over S}

   300	    {S X : Scheme.{u}} {π : X ⟶ S} [IsProper π] {T : Over S}
   301	    [IsLocallyNoetherian (T.left : Scheme.{u})] (x : Scheme.DivFamily π T)

   304	    ((Scheme.Modules.pushforward (pullback.snd π T.hom)).obj x.F).IsFinitePresentation := by
   305	  letI := x.isFinitePresentation
   306	  haveI := x.isQuasicoherent_pushforward
   307	  refine Scheme.Modules.isFinitePresentation_of_finite_sections _ (fun V hV => ?_)
   308	  let q := pullback.snd π T.hom
   309	  let i := Scheme.Modules.schematicSupportι x.F
   310	  haveI : IsProper (i ≫ q) := x.properSupport
   311	  haveI : IsFinite (i ≫ q) := IsFinite.of_isProper_of_locallyQuasiFinite _
   312	  haveI : IsAffineHom i :=
   313	    inferInstanceAs (IsAffineHom (Scheme.Modules.annihilator x.F).subschemeι)
   314	  let D := Scheme.Modules.schematicSupport x.F
   315	  let W : D.Opens := (i ≫ q) ⁻¹ᵁ V
   316	  let N : D.Modules := (Scheme.Modules.pullback i).obj x.F
   317	  haveI : N.IsFinitePresentation :=
   318	    Scheme.Modules.isFinitePresentation_pullback_schematicSupportι x.F x.isFinitePresentation
   319	  -- the finiteness tower over the affine `V`
   320	  letI : Algebra Γ(T.left, V) Γ(D, W) := (Scheme.Hom.app (i ≫ q) V).hom.toAlgebra
   321	  letI : Module Γ(T.left, V) Γ(N, W) :=
   322	    Module.compHom _ (Scheme.Hom.app (i ≫ q) V).hom
   323	  haveI : Module.Finite Γ(T.left, V) Γ(D, W) := IsFinite.finite_app (i ≫ q) V hV

   325	    Scheme.Modules.finite_sections_preimage_of_isAffineHom (i ≫ q) N hV
   326	  haveI : IsScalarTower Γ(T.left, V) Γ(D, W) Γ(N, W) :=
   327	    IsScalarTower.of_algebraMap_smul fun _ _ => rfl
   328	  haveI htrans : Module.Finite Γ(T.left, V) Γ(N, W) :=
   329	    Module.Finite.trans Γ(D, W) _

   335	      ((Scheme.Modules.pushforward q).map hdesc.inv).app V) =
   336	      𝟙 Γ((Scheme.Modules.pushforward q).obj x.F, V) := by
   337	    rw [← Scheme.Modules.Hom.comp_app, ← Functor.map_comp, hdesc.hom_inv_id]

   339	  refine Module.Finite.of_surjective
   340	    ({ toFun := fun n => ((Scheme.Modules.pushforward q).map hdesc.inv).app V n
   341	       map_add' := fun a b => map_add _ a b
   342	       map_smul' := fun r n =>
   343	         Scheme.Modules.Hom.app_smul
   344	           ((Scheme.Modules.pushforward q).map hdesc.inv) r n } :
   345	      Γ(N, W) →ₗ[Γ(T.left, V)]
   346	        Γ((Scheme.Modules.pushforward q).obj x.F, V)) (fun z => ?_)
   347	  exact ⟨((Scheme.Modules.pushforward q).map hdesc.hom).app V z,
   348	    congrArg (fun f => f z) hcomp⟩

The goal of the chapter is to record that such a module is coherent in the sense the Quot construction consumes, namely finitely presented: \(M.\mathtt{IsFinitePresentation}\) in Mathlib’s \(\mathtt{SheafOfModules.IsFinitePresentation}\) (built from a \(\mathtt{QuasicoherentData}\)). The mathematics is elementary: on each trivialising chart \(M|_U \cong \mathcal{O}_{U}\) is finite free of rank one, hence has the trivial finite presentation, and finite presentation is by definition a local condition. No stalk computation and no spreading-out are involved. The content is the bookkeeping that turns the pointwise trivialisation into the indexed \(\mathtt{QuasicoherentData}\) Mathlib expects.

They require, for every object \(x : C\), three instances on the slice topology \(J/x\) (Mathlib \(J.\mathtt{over}\ x\)):

/home/axel/LeanAlgebraicGeometry-Horizon/MainProjects/Algebraic-Jacobian-Challenge/blueprint/web/chap-Picard_LineBundleCoherence.html:1746:

For the ringed-space site underlying \(X\) with sheaf of rings \(R = X.\mathtt{ringCatSheaf}\), every slice topology \(J/x\) carries the three instances \(\mathtt{HasSheafCompose}\), \(\mathtt{HasWeakSheafify}\) and \(\mathtt{WEqualsLocallyBijective}\) (for the forgetful functor \(\mathrm{RingCat}\to \mathrm{AddCommGrpCat}\)) demanded by \(\mathtt{SheafOfModules.QuasicoherentData}\). Under this assumption the predicate \(M.\mathtt{IsFinitePresentation}\) is well-formed for every \(M : X.\mathtt{Modules}\).

/home/axel/LeanAlgebraicGeometry-Horizon/MainProjects/Algebraic-Jacobian-Challenge/blueprint/web/chap-Picard_LineBundleCoherence.html:2220:

[Locally trivial \(\Rightarrow \) finitely presented] Source: [Stacks Project], Tag 0B8M (Modules, Lemma 17.25.4). Let \(X\) be a scheme satisfying 900 and let \(M : X.\mathtt{Modules}\) be locally trivial, \(\texttt{IsLocallyTrivial}(M)\). Then \(M\) is finitely presented: \(M.\mathtt{IsFinitePresentation}\) holds in Mathlib’s \(\mathtt{SheafOfModules.IsFinitePresentation}\).

/home/axel/LeanAlgebraicGeometry-Horizon/MainProjects/Algebraic-Jacobian-Challenge/blueprint/web/chap-Picard_LineBundleCoherence.html:2232:

By 901 choose a trivialising affine cover \(\{ U_i\} _{i \in I}\) with isomorphisms \(e_i : M|_{U_i} \cong \mathcal{O}_{U_i}\). Assemble these into a \(\mathtt{QuasicoherentData}\) for \(M\): the index type is \(I\), the covering objects are the affine opens \(U_i\) (which cover \(X\)), and the presentation attached to index \(i\) is the finite free presentation of \(M|_{U_i}\) (equivalently, of the restriction \(M.\mathtt{over}\, U_i\)) produced in 905. Each such presentation is finite by 905; the assembled \(\mathtt{QuasicoherentData}\) therefore satisfies \(\mathtt{QuasicoherentData.IsFinitePresentation}\), and the constructor \(\mathtt{SheafOfModules.IsFinitePresentation.mk}\) yields \(M.\mathtt{IsFinitePresentation}\).

/home/axel/LeanAlgebraicGeometry-Horizon/MainProjects/Algebraic-Jacobian-Challenge/blueprint/web/chap-Picard_LineBundleCoherence.html:2301:

[Locally trivial \(\Rightarrow \) finite type] Under the hypotheses of 906, the locally trivial module \(M\) is of finite type (\(M.\mathtt{IsFiniteType}\)). Quasi-coherence (\(M.\mathtt{IsQuasicoherent}\)) follows from finite presentation via \(\mathtt{SheafOfModules.instIsQuasicoherentOfIsFinitePresentation}\).

/home/axel/LeanAlgebraicGeometry-Horizon/MainProjects/Algebraic-Jacobian-Challenge/blueprint/web/chap-Picard_LineBundleCoherence.html:2313:

Finite presentation implies finite type by Mathlib’s \(\mathtt{SheafOfModules.instIsFiniteTypeOfIsFinitePresentation}\), immediate from 906. Quasi-coherence is immediate from finite presentation by \(\mathtt{SheafOfModules.instIsQuasicoherentOfIsFinitePresentation}\).

    {S X : Scheme.{u}} {π : X ⟶ S} [IsProper π] {T : Over S}
    [IsLocallyNoetherian (T.left : Scheme.{u})] (x : Scheme.DivFamily π T)
    [LocallyQuasiFinite
      (Scheme.Modules.schematicSupportι x.F ≫ pullback.snd π T.hom)] :
    ((Scheme.Modules.pushforward (pullback.snd π T.hom)).obj x.F).IsFinitePresentation := by
  letI := x.isFinitePresentation
  haveI := x.isQuasicoherent_pushforward
  refine Scheme.Modules.isFinitePresentation_of_finite_sections _ (fun V hV => ?_)
  let q := pullback.snd π T.hom
  let i := Scheme.Modules.schematicSupportι x.F
  haveI : IsProper (i ≫ q) := x.properSupport
  haveI : IsFinite (i ≫ q) := IsFinite.of_isProper_of_locallyQuasiFinite _
  haveI : IsAffineHom i :=
    inferInstanceAs (IsAffineHom (Scheme.Modules.annihilator x.F).subschemeι)
  let D := Scheme.Modules.schematicSupport x.F
  let W : D.Opens := (i ≫ q) ⁻¹ᵁ V
  let N : D.Modules := (Scheme.Modules.pullback i).obj x.F
  haveI : N.IsFinitePresentation :=
    Scheme.Modules.isFinitePresentation_pullback_schematicSupportι x.F x.isFinitePresentation
  -- the finiteness tower over the affine `V`
  letI : Algebra Γ(T.left, V) Γ(D, W) := (Scheme.Hom.app (i ≫ q) V).hom.toAlgebra
  letI : Module Γ(T.left, V) Γ(N, W) :=
    Module.compHom _ (Scheme.Hom.app (i ≫ q) V).hom
  haveI : Module.Finite Γ(T.left, V) Γ(D, W) := IsFinite.finite_app (i ≫ q) V hV
  haveI : Module.Finite Γ(D, W) Γ(N, W) :=
    Scheme.Modules.finite_sections_preimage_of_isAffineHom (i ≫ q) N hV
  haveI : IsScalarTower Γ(T.left, V) Γ(D, W) Γ(N, W) :=
    IsScalarTower.of_algebraMap_smul fun _ _ => rfl
  haveI htrans : Module.Finite Γ(T.left, V) Γ(N, W) :=
    Module.Finite.trans Γ(D, W) _
  -- transport along the descent isomorphism; both `Γ`-identifications are `rfl`
  have hdesc : x.F ≅ (Scheme.Modules.pushforward i).obj N :=
    Scheme.Modules.schematicSupportDescentIso x.F

  have hcomp : (((Scheme.Modules.pushforward q).map hdesc.hom).app V ≫
      ((Scheme.Modules.pushforward q).map hdesc.inv).app V) =
      𝟙 Γ((Scheme.Modules.pushforward q).obj x.F, V) := by
    rw [← Scheme.Modules.Hom.comp_app, ← Functor.map_comp, hdesc.hom_inv_id]
    simp
  refine Module.Finite.of_surjective
    ({ toFun := fun n => ((Scheme.Modules.pushforward q).map hdesc.inv).app V n
       map_add' := fun a b => map_add _ a b
       map_smul' := fun r n =>
         Scheme.Modules.Hom.app_smul
           ((Scheme.Modules.pushforward q).map hdesc.inv) r n } :
      Γ(N, W) →ₗ[Γ(T.left, V)]
        Γ((Scheme.Modules.pushforward q).obj x.F, V)) (fun z => ?_)
  exact ⟨((Scheme.Modules.pushforward q).map hdesc.hom).app V z,
    congrArg (fun f => f z) hcomp⟩---

docstring: '**Serre finiteness in engine-ready form** (companion to

  `sectionGradedModule_fg`; `lem:sectionGradedModule_fg`, [Nitsure] §1): for

  `π : X ⟶ S` projective carrying the very ample line bundle `L` and a coherent

  (finitely presented) sheaf `F`, the graded Hilbert function

  `m ↦ dim_{κ(s)} Γ(X_s, F_s ⊗ L_s^{⊗m})` at each fibre over `s : S` is packaged by

  a `GradedHilbert` datum over the residue field `κ(s)`.


  NAMED LEAF (`sorry`): this is `sectionGradedModule_fg` (Serre) restated in the

  form the graded Hilbert–Serre rationality engine consumes.  Taking `M` to be the

  fibre section module `⊕ₘ Γ(X_s, F_s ⊗ L_s^{⊗m})` and the `d+1` generators to be

  the coordinate sections of the very-ample embedding `X_s ↪ ℙ^d`, its content is

  the finite generation of that module over the homogeneous coordinate ring

  `κ(s)[x₀,…,x_d]` — the `MvPolynomial` reshaping documented in inbox `I-0109`.

  Compared with the abstract-section-ring finiteness of `sectionGradedModule_fg`,

  this form additionally records the degree-one coordinate action, which is what

  makes the Hilbert polynomial genuine

  (`hilbertPolynomial_eval_eventually_of_projective`).'

/-! ## Finite generation of affine sections (Stacks 01PC, finite-type half)

For a sheaf of modules of finite presentation `F` on a scheme `X`
(Mathlib's `SheafOfModules.IsFinitePresentation`), the module of sections
`Γ(F, V)` over any affine open `V` contained in a member of the presenting
cover is a *finite* `Γ(X, V)`-module.  This is the chart-level input that
Nitsure §4 generic flatness (`AlgebraicGeometry.genericFlatness`, file
`GenericFlatnessGeometric.lean`) feeds to the algebraic generic-freeness
theorem `GenericFreeness.genericFlatnessAlgebraic`.

Route (every bridge already exists in this file):
1. the slice generating sections of `F.over (q.X i)` geometrize across the
   slice-to-geometric equivalence (`overRestrictEquiv` / `overRestrictPullbackIso`,
   via Mathlib's `GeneratingSections.map`) to the open subscheme `(q.X i).toScheme`;
2. they pull back along the open-immersion factorization
   `k : Spec Γ(X, V) ⟶ (q.X i).toScheme` of `hV.fromSpec` (unit datum
   `pullbackOpenImmersionUnitIso`), and the pseudofunctor isos
   `pullbackComp`/`pullbackCongr` carry them onto `(pullback hV.fromSpec).obj F`;
3. the Stacks 01I8 identification `tildeIso_of_isQuasicoherent_isAffineOpen`
   lands them on `tilde Γ(F, V)`;
4. a finite generating epimorphism onto a tilde forces finite generation of the
   underlying module (`module_finite_of_tilde_genSections`): transposing the
   epimorphism through the tilde–Γ adjunction gives a module map out of a finite
   free module which is epi, because the adjunction counit at a tilde is
   invertible and `tilde.functor` is faithful. -/

    15	A finite morphism to the projective line supplies finite Laurent two-chart
    16	data, hence a closed immersion into a relative projective space.  The existing

    33	/-- A proper scheme admitting a finite morphism to the projective line is

    36	    (C : Over (Spec (CommRingCat.of k)))

events.text: I’m keeping the theorem as a useful conditional bridge rather than silently broadening its scope: the existing project explicitly records that support quasi-finiteness has no producer, and the noetherian coherence route is the only available finite-presentation producer. I’ll add those limits to the source docstrings, plus the universe-0 limitation of `IsProjectiveWith`, then update the roadmap handoff with the same precise boundary.
